text:
About 400,000 guests have attended a wedding hosted by a politician in India’s poorest state, choking roads and sending spectators scrambling up electricity pylons for a glimpse of the lavish celebrations.
Anant Singh, a six-time MP who is facing dozens of criminal cases including murder charges, invited villagers, political allies and VIPs to his daughter’s wedding in the eastern state of Bihar on Wednesday. Singh denies any wrongdoing regarding the charges he faces.
The scale of the event was staggering even by the standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings, which usually last for days.
Guests were treated to 500,000 pieces of traditional sweets, and a vegetarian feast prepared by an army of 500 chefs and cooks, Singh’s confidant Munna Singh told AFP.
The event in Singh’s home village of Nadawan drew such huge crowds that roads leading to the venue ground to a standstill.
One politician, unable to force his way through the traffic chaos, abandoned his car and rode a tractor across farm fields to reach the venue, the Times of India reported.
Organisers built five helipads to ferry in VIP guests, with each helicopter touchdown whipping up clouds of dust that swept through crowds of curious onlookers.
Images published by the Press Trust of India news agency showed thousands of people jostling for a glimpse of the sprawling venue, while others perched precariously atop trees and electricity towers.
Organisers were forced to postpone a horse race as part of the celebrations after about 100,000 people turned up to watch the spectacle, which involved 200 horses.
Guests were also treated to elaborate flower arrangements featuring blooms imported from China and a fireworks display.
The bride, Shivangi Singh, arrived in a luxury BMW, while the groom, Rishikesh Kumar, travelled in a convoy of about 200 cars.
More than 10m weddings take place in India every year, feeding an industry estimated to be worth $40-$50bn, according to KPMG.
